overview: Barbados is an island country in the eastern Caribbean, the most easterly of the Caribbean islands. Its capital is Bridgetown. Barbados became independent from the United Kingdom in 1966, and in 2021 it became a republic, replacing the British monarch with its own president. It is known for cricket, rum and its beaches.

geography.text: Barbados is a fairly flat island made mostly of coral limestone, with gentle hills rising in the centre. The calm west coast faces the Caribbean Sea and has sandy beaches, while the rougher east coast faces the open Atlantic. Coral reefs surround much of the island.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical and sunny, with a rainy season from June to November.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Green monkeys, brought from West Africa centuries ago, live in the gullies; turtles nest on the beaches.

history.text: English settlers arrived in Barbados in 1627 and turned it into one of the richest sugar colonies in the world, worked by enslaved Africans. Slavery ended in 1834. Barbados became independent in 1966, and in 2021 it became a republic with its own president.

events.title: Republic
events.text: Barbados replaces the British monarch with an elected president.

government.text: Barbados is a parliamentary republic. In 2021 it removed the British monarch as head of state and elected its first President, Sandra Mason. The Prime Minister leads the government. Parliament has an elected House of Assembly, which has sat since 1639, making it one of the oldest in the Commonwealth.

economy.text: Tourism is Barbados's main industry, along with offshore finance. Sugar was once everything; Barbados was the first British colony where sugar plantations took off. It still makes rum: Mount Gay claims to be the oldest rum brand in the world.

culture.text: Crop Over, a festival marking the end of the sugar harvest, is Barbados's biggest celebration, with calypso and soca music. The singer Rihanna, from Bridgetown, was named a National Hero in 2021. Bridgetown's historic centre and its garrison are a UNESCO site.

items.title: Crop Over
items.text: A summer festival that grew from the end of the sugar harvest.

items.title: Rihanna
items.text: The singer and businesswoman, a National Hero of Barbados.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Cou-cou and flying fish is the national dish. Rum has been made on the island since the 1600s.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Calypso and soca music, and global stars such as Rihanna.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Crop Over, the summer festival, began as a celebration of the end of the sugar cane harvest.

sport.text: Cricket is the national sport, and Barbados has produced many West Indies greats, including Garfield Sobers, often called the best all-rounder of all time. Kensington Oval hosted the 2007 and 2024 Cricket World Cup finals.

items.title: Garfield Sobers
items.text: Hit six sixes in one over in 1968.

items.title: Kensington Oval
items.text: Hosted the 2007 World Cup and 2024 T20 World Cup finals.

didYouKnow: George Washington visited Barbados in 1751, the only time he ever left mainland North America.
The grapefruit is thought to have first appeared in Barbados in the 1700s.
